label: text
text: A Chinese boatman was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy this morning with using obscene language.

label: text
text: The complainant, Mr. E. L. Stainfield, stated in evidence that he was travelling by the "Star" ferry from Kowloon to Hongkong on Saturday afternoon and in the middle of the harbour the accused used an indecent expression after posting himself at the rear of a passing junk. Witness later engaged a motor boat and in company with his wife and Mr. W. Anderson of the Naval Hospital overhauled the junk near Arsenal Street. Witness stated that the accused jumped into the harbour as soon as he boarded the junk and repeated the expression used.

label: text
text: Accused denied that he used the alleged expression, and explained his fall into the sea by stating that he was assaulted by the complainant and pushed overboard.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned until to-morrow for the examination of other witnesses.

text: Mr. A. M. Powell, after a visit to China and Japan this spring, writes to The Times blaming the cinematograph as the main cause of the present unrest. He says: The worst and cheapest sort of American films were everywhere shown, and the Chinese were taking to it like ducks to water, the result being (a very natural) contempt for Europe and America in general.

label: text
text: Progress in the Hongkong Baseball League was resumed on Saturday afternoon, after a brief interval caused both by the strike and by the inclement weather.

label: text
text: As events turned out each of the two games were very one-sided.

label: text
text: In the first match the Hong-kong Volunteers were opposed by the Japanese, the latter having an easy win by 16-4.

label: text
text: The second game proved almost a repetition of the first so far as the debacle of one of the opposing teams was concerned, the Hongkong Baseball Club accounting for the defeat of the Indian Recreation Club by a formidable total of 19-5.

label: text
text: The scores in catch instance, it will be admitted, speak for themselves, and it would be superfluous to describe either match in detail.

label: text
text: The baseballers, however, are to be complimented on setting the lead in the matter of resumption of Saturday afternoon sport in spite of the strike, and now that they have shown the way there is no doubt that other forms of sport will be revived. It is admitted that many of our sportsmen are having rather strenuous times during the week, but that is only an additional reason for the opportunity being afford-ed them of having some form of healthy relaxation on Saturday afternoons.

label: text
text: Canada has lost one of its most widely known men in the person of Mr. G. M. Bosworth who died in London yesterday.

label: text
text: Cable advice of his death was received by the local office of the Canadian Pacific Steamships Ltd. of which large concern he was the Chairman.

label: text
text: At the time of his death the late Mr. Bosworth was on one of his trips in connection with the Company's interests. His age was 67.

label: text
text: The late Mr. Bosworth entered transportation service in 1875, joining the Canadian Pacific Railway Company in 1882. After holding a number of important traffic positions on the Rail Lines, he was, in 1901, appointed Fourth Vice-President In Charge of Rail Traffic; in 1910 he was appointed Vice-President In Charge of Traffic, Rail and Steamships. In 1918, owing to the growth of the Canadian Pacific Steamship interests on the Pacific and Atlantic, Mr. Bosworth was appointed Chairman, Canadian Pacific Ocean Services, Ltd. (now Canadian Pacific Steamships, Ltd.), which position he held up to the time of his death.

label: text
text: Mr. Bosworth leaves a widow and two children—a son and a daughter.
